Because only one library exists per condition, all findings are descriptive and require validation with replicated experiments.

---

## 1. Introduction

DDX41 is an RNA-binding protein involved in RNA processing and translation. Mutations in DDX41 have been associated with retinal degeneration. The present analysis characterizes the transcriptional landscape of the DDX41 mutant retina relative to WT at single-cell resolution, with the goal of identifying cell-type-specific and pan-retinal transcriptional changes that may underlie the degenerative phenotype.

---

## 2. Methods

### 2.1 Data and quality control

The dataset is a single-cell RNA-seq AnnData object (Ddx41_DEG.h5ad) containing 15,307 cells and 33,696 genes. Cells were filtered using the following thresholds: minimum 200 detected genes, maximum 10% mitochondrial read percentage, and singlet classification only (all 15,307 cells were classified as singlets). After gene-level filtering (minimum 3 cells), 22,387 genes remained. The top 2,000 highly variable genes were selected for downstream dimensionality reduction. Counts were log1p-transformed for normalization. All analyses were executed on an HPC cluster via SLURM (execution_mode: hpc_slurm).

### 2.2 Stratified differential expression

A Wilcoxon rank-sum test (tie-corrected) was computed comparing DDX41 mutant cells against WT cells within each major class. Parameters: minimum detection in 10% of one population (min_pct = 0.1), log₂ fold-change threshold of 0.25 (lfc = 0.25), no FDR cutoff applied (padj threshold = 1.0, reflecting the absence of biological replicates). The top 50 genes per direction per group were retained for reporting. Because cells within a major class are subsamples of a single donor per condition, Wilcoxon scores and log₂FC values are reported as descriptive, exploratory rank metrics only.

### 2.3 Cell composition

The fraction of cells belonging to each major class was computed per condition (sampleid). With one library per condition, proportions are reported descriptively without statistical testing.

### 2.4 Clustering

Leiden clustering was performed on the top 30 principal components with a neighborhood graph of 15 neighbors per cell. The resolution was selected by bootstrap stability (10 bootstraps, minimum stability 0.9), yielding resolution = 0.2 and 20 clusters (stability = 0.9605, SD = 0.0081).

### 2.5 Pathway over-representation analysis (ORA)

Over-representation analysis was performed against three local gene-set libraries: GO_Biological_Process_2023 (5,407 terms), Reactome_2022 (1,818 terms), and MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (50 terms). Genes were selected per cell type and direction using padj < 0.05 and |log₂FC| ≥ 0.25. The background was the tested universe of 11,293 genes (genes passing the min_pct filter in at least one group). The top 10 enriched terms per subset were reported.

### 2.6 Preranked gene-set enrichment analysis (GSEA)

Preranked GSEA was performed using the complete Wilcoxon-ranked gene lists (ranking statistic: wilcoxon_z) for each major class. Parameters: minimum gene set size 15, maximum 500, 1,000 permutations, seed 42, FDR threshold 0.05. Signed Normalized Enrichment Scores (NES) and FDR q-values were reported.

### 2.7 Cross-cell-type synthesis

Genes meeting the |log₂FC| ≥ 0.25 criterion in each major class were aggregated. A consensus ranking metric (|log₂FC| × fraction of groups in which the gene was expressed in the same direction) was computed to identify pan-retinal signatures.

---

## 3. Results

### 3.1 Dataset overview and quality control

After QC filtering, all 15,307 cells were retained (0% removed; all cells passed the ≥200 genes, ≤10% mt, and singlet criteria). Gene-level filtering reduced the feature set from 33,696 to 22,387 genes. The dataset comprises 9,047 WT cells and 6,260 DDX41 mutant cells. All cells were classified as singlets (DF.classifications = "Singlet" for all 15,307 cells), and orig.ident contained a single value (0) for all cells, confirming one biological library per condition.

Descriptive QC metrics:

| Metric | WT | DDX41 |
|--------|-----|-------|
| Cell count | 9,047 | 6,260 |
| Mean nFeature_RNA | 1,504.6 | 2,075.8 |
| Median nFeature_RNA | 1,194.0 | 1,776.5 |

The DDX41 arm shows higher mean and median gene detection per cell, which may reflect a shift in cell-type composition toward populations with higher transcriptomic complexity (e.g., reactive glia) or a genuine increase in transcriptional output.

| Rod | 66.02 | 65.24 | 0.99 | −0.78 |
| BC | 18.88 | 12.80 | 0.68 | −6.08 |
| MG | 5.91 | 12.57 | 2.13 | +6.66 |
| Cone | 5.52 | 1.79 | 0.32 | −3.73 |

**AC (Amacrine cells).** The strongest up-regulated gene was Angpt1 (log₂FC = +2.58). The strongest down-regulated gene was Apoe (log₂FC = −4.91). **BC (Bipolar cells).** The strongest up-regulated gene was Xlr3b (log₂FC = +3.83). Immune/inflammatory genes were prominently up-regulated (A2m +3.32, C4b, Serping1 family). ### 3.4 Clustering

Leiden clustering at resolution 0.2 (selected by bootstrap stability = 0.9605) yielded 20 clusters. The two largest clusters (0: 6,199 cells; 1: 3,738 cells) together account for 64% of all cells. | A2m | Up | Up +++ | — | Up | — | Acute-phase response |

---

## 4. Discussion

The DDX41 mutant retina exhibits a coherent, multi-layered transcriptional reorganization that can be summarized in three interlocking themes:

**Theme 1: Pan-retinal translational up-regulation.** The most consistent signal across all five tested cell types is the up-regulation of translation-related pathways. In ORA, terms such as Cytoplasmic Translation (GO:0002181), Eukaryotic Translation Elongation R-HSA-156842, and Peptide Chain Elongation R-HSA-156902 appear in the top 10 for AC, BC, MG, and Rod. In preranked GSEA, these same terms carry the highest positive NES values (ranging from +2.47 to +3.48) with FDR = 0.0 in every group. The pan-retinal up-regulation of Hmgn2 (5/5 groups), Ubb (5/5), and Rps20 (5/5) in the cross-cell-type synthesis further supports a global translational stress response. This is consistent with DDX41's known role in RNA processing and translation: loss of DDX41 function may trigger a compensatory up-regulation of the translational machinery or a stress-induced translational reprogramming.

**Theme 2: Phototransduction collapse and metabolic shift in photoreceptors.** Rods show the most dramatic down-regulation of phototransduction pathways: Visual Phototransduction R-HSA-2187338 (NES = −4.25), Phototransduction Cascade R-HSA-2514856 (NES = −4.12), and Inactivation, Recovery And Regulation Of Phototransduction Cascade R-HSA-2514859 (NES = −4.00) are the three most strongly down-regulated pathways in the entire dataset. Simultaneously, rods up-regulate extracellular matrix/injury-response genes (Col25a1, log₂FC = +8.74) and mitochondrial electron transport (NES = +2.44). Cones, while proportionally depleted (5.52% → 1.79%), mount a predominantly up-regulated programme (47 of 50 top up-genes at |log₂FC| ≥ 1.0) led by Cartpt (+5.99) and Oxidative Phosphorylation, while down-regulating glycolysis and hypoxia pathways. This suggests that surviving cones shift toward oxidative metabolism as a survival strategy, while rods undergo a more severe degenerative/fibrotic transformation.

**Theme 3: Reactive gliosis and neuroinflammation.** The 2.13-fold expansion of MG in the DDX41 mutant is accompanied by massive up-regulation of Gfap (+6.02), complement components (C4b, Serping1, A2m), and translation machinery. The down-regulation of synaptic and adhesion pathways in MG (Nervous System Development, Cell-Cell Adhesion, Axon Guidance, Synapse Assembly) is consistent with a shift from a homeostatic to a reactive glial state. BC cells show a parallel but less extreme inflammatory activation (Xlr3b +3.83, A2m +3.32, immediate-early genes Fos/Egr1/Junb), suggesting that the neuroinflammatory response is not confined to glia but extends to interneurons.

**Composition–expression concordance.** The expansion of MG and AC in the DDX41 mutant is concordant with their up-regulated stress/inflammatory transcriptional profiles. The contraction of BC and Cone is concordant with their respective inflammatory activation (BC) and survival programme (Cone). The stability of Rod proportion despite dramatic transcriptional change suggests that at this timepoint, rods are transcriptionally altered but not yet proportionally lost—a finding that may reflect an early stage of degeneration.

---

## 5. Limitations

1. **Single library per condition.** There is one biological library for WT and one for DDX41. No valid statistical test for replicability exists. All p-values, FDR values, and NES scores are descriptive/exploratory metrics, not inferential evidence of differential expression. The Wilcoxon scores and log₂FC values should be interpreted as effect-size rankings only.

2. **No FDR correction for the DE contrast.** Because padj was set to 1.0 (no FDR cutoff), the "significant" gene counts reported (e.g., 3,971 in AC) reflect the |log₂FC| ≥ 0.25 threshold only, not a multiple-testing correction.

3. **Six cell classes not analyzed.** Endothelial, HC, Microglia, Pericyte, RGC, and RPE were excluded from the stratified DE analysis because fewer than 30 cells were present in at least one arm. No findings can be drawn for these populations.

4. **Pseudoreplication.** Cells within a major class are subsamples of a single donor. The Wilcoxon rank-sum test compares cells within one donor against cells within another, which does not constitute a valid test of between-donor differences.

5. **Composition confounding.** Because cell-type proportions shift between conditions (e.g., MG doubles, Cone is depleted by 3-fold), any pooled (unstratified) differential expression result would be confounded by composition. The stratified design mitigates this, but the composition shift itself means that the DDX41 mutant retina is not simply "the same cells with different expression" but a reorganized tissue.

6. **Single timepoint.** The analysis captures a snapshot; temporal dynamics of the degenerative process are not resolved.

---

## 6. Conclusions

The DDX41 mutant retina displays a transcriptional reorganization characterized by: (i) a pan-retinal up-regulation of translation-related pathways across all five tested cell types; (ii) a severe collapse of phototransduction in rods (NES up to −4.25) accompanied by an extracellular matrix/injury response; (iii) a compensatory oxidative-metabolism survival programme in surviving cones; (iv) a massive reactive gliosis in Müller glia (Gfap +6.02) with concurrent neuroinflammatory activation in bipolar cells; and (v) a compositional shift toward glial and amacrine populations at the expense of bipolar and cone populations. These findings are descriptive and exploratory, generated from a single library per condition, and should be interpreted as hypotheses to be validated with replicated experiments, orthogonal assays (e.g., RNA-FISH, protein-level confirmation), and time-course designs.

---

## Data and Code Availability

All analyses were executed on an HPC cluster (SLURM). Checkpoints (adata_qc.h5ad, adata_de.h5ad, adata_clustered.h5ad), DE tables, enrichment tables, composition tables, and figures are available in the artifacts directory.

    - `min_cells` = `3` — drop a gene detected in fewer cells than this — too sparse to support any test

Raise it only for a tissue known to be mitochondria-rich, and say so
    - `n_top_genes` = `2000` — how many highly-variable genes to keep for the embedding — more genes carry more structure and more noise. 2000 is Seurat's default and the usual starting point

### Pathway enrichment

Over-representation analysis (ORA) and preranked gene-set enrichment analysis (GSEA) were performed to identify coordinated pathway-level changes.

**Pan-retinal translational up-regulation.** The most consistent signal across all five tested cell types is the up-regulation of translation-related pathways. In ORA, terms such as Cytoplasmic Translation (GO:0002181), Eukaryotic Translation Elongation (R-HSA-156842), and Peptide Chain Elongation (R-HSA-156902) appear in the top 10 for AC, BC, MG, and Rod. In preranked GSEA, these same terms carry the highest positive NES values (ranging from +2.47 to +3.48) with FDR = 0.0 in every group. The pan-retinal up-regulation of Hmgn2 (5/5 groups), Ubb (5/5), and Rps20 (5/5) in the cross-cell-type synthesis further supports a global translational stress response.

**Phototransduction collapse in rods.** Rods show the most dramatic down-regulation of phototransduction pathways in the entire dataset: Visual Phototransduction (R-HSA-2187338, NES = −4.25), Phototransduction Cascade (R-HSA-2514856, NES = −4.12), and Inactivation, Recovery And Regulation Of Phototransduction Cascade (R-HSA-2514859, NES = −4.00). Simultaneously, rods up-regulate extracellular matrix/injury-response genes and mitochondrial electron transport (NES = +2.44). Cones, while proportionally depleted, mount a predominantly up-regulated programme led by Oxidative Phosphorylation, while down-regulating glycolysis (NES = −2.87), carbohydrate catabolic process (NES = −2.90), and hypoxia (NES = −2.59). This suggests that surviving cones shift toward oxidative metabolism as a survival strategy, while rods undergo a more severe degenerative/fibrotic transformation.

**Reactive gliosis and neuroinflammation.** The 2.13-fold expansion of MG is accompanied by massive up-regulation of Gfap (+6.02), complement components (C4b, Serping1, A2m), and translation machinery. The down-regulation of synaptic and adhesion pathways in MG (Nervous System Development, Cell-Cell Adhesion, Axon Guidance, Synapse Assembly) is consistent with a shift from a homeostatic to a reactive glial state. Gfap, C4b, and A2m were up-regulated in multiple cell types, linking the reactive gliosis and neuroinflammatory themes across the retina.

## Discussion

The DDX41 mutant retina exhibits a coherent, multi-layered transcriptional reorganization that can be summarized in three interlocking themes. First, a pan-retinal translational up-regulation is the most consistent signal across all five tested cell types, consistent with DDX41's known role in RNA processing and translation: loss of DDX41 function may trigger a compensatory up-regulation of the translational machinery or a stress-induced translational reprogramming. Second, photoreceptors undergo divergent fates: rods experience a severe collapse of phototransduction (NES up to −4.25) accompanied by an extracellular matrix/injury response, while surviving cones mount a compensatory oxidative-metabolism survival programme. Third, reactive gliosis and neuroinflammation are prominent, with Müller glia showing massive Gfap up-regulation and complement activation, and bipolar cells showing a parallel inflammatory activation. The composition–expression concordance is notable: the expansion of MG and AC is concordant with their up-regulated stress/inflammatory transcriptional profiles, while the contraction of BC and Cone is concordant with their respective inflammatory activation and survival programmes. The stability of rod proportion despite dramatic transcriptional change suggests that at this timepoint, rods are transcriptionally altered but not yet proportionally lost—a finding that may reflect an early stage of degeneration.

## Limitations

1. **Single library per condition.** There is one biological library for WT and one for DDX41. No valid statistical test for replicability exists. All p-values, FDR values, and NES scores are descriptive/exploratory metrics, not inferential evidence of differential expression. The Wilcoxon scores and log₂FC values should be interpreted as effect-size rankings only.

2. **No FDR correction for the DE contrast.** Because padj was set to 1.0 (no FDR cutoff), the "significant" gene counts reported reflect the |log₂FC| ≥ 0.25 threshold only, not a multiple-testing correction.

3. **Six cell classes not analyzed.** Endothelial, HC, Microglia, Pericyte, RGC, and RPE were excluded from the stratified DE analysis because fewer than 30 cells were present in at least one arm. No findings can be drawn for these populations.

4. **Pseudoreplication.** Cells within a major class are subsamples of a single donor. The Wilcoxon rank-sum test compares cells within one donor against cells within another, which does not constitute a valid test of between-donor differences.

5. **Composition confounding.** Because cell-type proportions shift between conditions (e.g., MG doubles, Cone is depleted by 3-fold), any pooled (unstratified) differential expression result would be confounded by composition. The stratified design mitigates this, but the composition shift itself means that the DDX41 mutant retina is not simply "the same cells with different expression" but a reorganized tissue.

6. **Single timepoint.** The analysis captures a snapshot; temporal dynamics of the degenerative process are not resolved.

## Conclusion

We performed a descriptive single-cell RNA-seq analysis of the DDX41 mutant retina relative to wild-type, identifying a pan-retinal up-regulation of translation-related pathways, a severe collapse of phototransduction in rods, a compensatory oxidative-metabolism survival programme in cones, and a massive reactive gliosis in Müller glia. The principal finding is that the DDX41 mutant retina is not merely a collection of cells with altered expression but a reorganized tissue in which composition shifts and cell-type-specific transcriptional programmes are tightly coupled. The next step is validation of these findings with replicated biological libraries, orthogonal assays (e.g., RNA-FISH, protein-level confirmation), and time-course designs to resolve the temporal dynamics of degeneration.

## Methods

1. **Dataset.** A single-cell RNA-seq AnnData object (Ddx41_DEG.h5ad) containing 15,307 cells and 33,696 genes was used. The dataset comprises 9,047 WT cells and 6,260 DDX41 mutant cells, with one biological library per condition (orig.ident = 0 for all cells). All cells carried pre-existing major-class and cell-type annotations spanning 11 retinal major classes.

2. **Quality control.** Cells were filtered using the following thresholds: minimum 200 detected genes per cell, maximum 10% mitochondrial read percentage, and singlet classification only. All 15,307 cells passed (0% removed). Gene-level filtering (minimum 3 cells) reduced the feature set from 33,696 to 22,387 genes.

3. **Normalization and highly variable gene selection.** Counts were log1p-transformed for normalization. The top 2,000 highly variable genes were selected for downstream dimensionality reduction.

4. **Dimensionality reduction.** Principal component analysis was performed on the normalized, highly variable gene matrix. The top 30 principal components were retained for downstream analyses.

5. **Neighbour graph construction.** A k-nearest-neighbour graph was constructed with 15 neighbours per cell on the 30-dimensional PCA space.

6. **Clustering.** Leiden clustering was performed on the neighbour graph. The resolution was selected by bootstrap stability (10 bootstraps, minimum stability threshold 0.9), yielding resolution = 0.2 and 20 clusters (stability = 0.9605, SD = 0.0081). The existing major-class and cell-type annotations were retained for all downstream analyses; de-novo cluster identifiers were used only for visualization.

7. **Stratified differential expression.** A Wilcoxon rank-sum test (tie-corrected) was computed comparing DDX41 mutant cells against WT cells within each major class. Parameters: minimum detection in 10% of one population (min_pct = 0.1), log₂ fold-change threshold of 0.25 (lfc = 0.25), no FDR cutoff applied (padj threshold = 1.0, reflecting the absence of biological replicates). The top 50 genes per direction per group were retained for reporting. Five of eleven major classes were tested (AC, BC, Cone, MG, Rod); six were excluded due to fewer than 30 cells in at least one arm.

8. **Cell composition.** The fraction of cells belonging to each major class was computed per condition (sampleid). With one library per condition, proportions are reported descriptively without statistical testing.

9. **Pathway over-representation analysis (ORA).** ORA was performed against three local gene-set libraries: GO_Biological_Process_2023 (5,407 terms), Reactome_2022 (1,818 terms), and MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (50 terms). Genes were selected per cell type and direction using padj < 0.05 and |log₂FC| ≥ 0.25. The background was the tested universe of 11,293 genes (genes passing the min_pct filter in at least one group). The top 10 enriched terms per subset were reported.

10. **Preranked gene-set enrichment analysis (GSEA).** Preranked GSEA was performed using the complete Wilcoxon-ranked gene lists (ranking statistic: wilcoxon_z) for each major class. Parameters: minimum gene set size 15, maximum 500, 1,000 permutations, seed 42, FDR threshold 0.05. Signed Normalized Enrichment Scores (NES) and FDR q-values were reported.

11. **Cross-cell-type synthesis.** Genes meeting the |log₂FC| ≥ 0.25 criterion in each major class were aggregated. A consensus ranking metric (|log₂FC| × fraction of groups in which the gene was expressed in the same direction) was computed to identify pan-retinal signatures.

All p-values, FDR values, and NES scores are descriptive/exploratory metrics, not inferential evidence of differential expression. The Wilcoxon scores and log₂FC values should be interpreted as effect-size rankings only.

2. **No FDR correction for the DE contrast.** Because padj was set to 1.0 (no FDR cutoff), the "significant" gene counts reported reflect the |log₂FC| ≥ 0.25 threshold only, not a multiple-testing correction.

3. **Six cell classes not analyzed.** Endothelial, HC, Microglia, Pericyte, RGC, and RPE were excluded from the stratified DE analysis because fewer than 30 cells were present in at least one arm. No findings can be drawn for these populations.

4. **Pseudoreplication.** Cells within a major class are subsamples of a single donor. The Wilcoxon rank-sum test compares cells within one donor against cells within another, which does not constitute a valid test of between-donor differences.

5. **Composition confounding.** Because cell-type proportions shift between conditions (e.g., MG doubles, Cone is depleted by 3-fold), any pooled (unstratified) differential expression result would be confounded by composition. The stratified design mitigates this, but the composition shift itself means that the DDX41 mutant retina is not simply "the same cells with different expression" but a reorganized tissue.

6. **Single timepoint.** The analysis captures a snapshot; temporal dynamics of the degenerative process are not resolved.

## Conclusion

We performed a descriptive single-cell RNA-seq analysis of the DDX41 mutant retina relative to wild-type, identifying a pan-retinal up-regulation of translation-related pathways, a severe collapse of phototransduction in rods, a compensatory oxidative-metabolism survival programme in cones, and a massive reactive gliosis in Müller glia. The principal finding is that the DDX41 mutant retina is not merely a collection of cells with altered expression but a reorganized tissue in which composition shifts and cell-type-specific transcriptional programmes are tightly coupled. The next step is validation of these findings with replicated biological libraries, orthogonal assays (e.g., RNA-FISH, protein-level confirmation), and time-course designs to resolve the temporal dynamics of degeneration.

## Methods

1. **Dataset.** A single-cell RNA-seq AnnData object (Ddx41_DEG.h5ad) containing 15,307 cells and 33,696 genes was used. The dataset comprises 9,047 WT cells and 6,260 DDX41 mutant cells, with one biological library per condition (orig.ident = 0 for all cells). All cells carried pre-existing major-class and cell-type annotations spanning 11 retinal major classes.

2. **Quality control.** Cells were filtered using the following thresholds: minimum 200 detected genes per cell, maximum 10% mitochondrial read percentage, and singlet classification only. All 15,307 cells passed (0% removed). Gene-level filtering (minimum 3 cells) reduced the feature set from 33,696 to 22,387 genes.

3. **Normalization and highly variable gene selection.** Counts were log1p-transformed for normalization. The top 2,000 highly variable genes were selected for downstream dimensionality reduction.

4. **Dimensionality reduction.** Principal component analysis was performed on the normalized, highly variable gene matrix. The top 30 principal components were retained for downstream analyses.

5. **Neighbour graph construction.** A k-nearest-neighbour graph was constructed with 15 neighbours per cell on the 30-dimensional PCA space.

6. **Clustering.** Leiden clustering was performed on the neighbour graph. The resolution was selected by bootstrap stability (10 bootstraps, minimum stability threshold 0.9), yielding resolution = 0.2 and 20 clusters (stability = 0.9605, SD = 0.0081). The existing major-class and cell-type annotations were retained for all downstream analyses; de-novo cluster identifiers were used only for visualization.

7. **Stratified differential expression.** A Wilcoxon rank-sum test (tie-corrected) was computed comparing DDX41 mutant cells against WT cells within each major class. Parameters: minimum detection in 10% of one population (min_pct = 0.1), log₂ fold-change threshold of 0.25 (lfc = 0.25), no FDR cutoff applied (padj threshold = 1.0, reflecting the absence of biological replicates). The top 50 genes per direction per group were retained for reporting. Five of eleven major classes were tested (AC, BC, Cone, MG, Rod); six were excluded due to fewer than 30 cells in at least one arm.

8. **Cell composition.** The fraction of cells belonging to each major class was computed per condition (sampleid). With one library per condition, proportions are reported descriptively without statistical testing.

9. **Pathway over-representation analysis (ORA).** ORA was performed against three local gene-set libraries: GO_Biological_Process_2023 (5,407 terms), Reactome_2022 (1,818 terms), and MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (50 terms). Genes were selected per cell type and direction using padj < 0.05 and |log₂FC| ≥ 0.25. The background was the tested universe of 11,293 genes (genes passing the min_pct filter in at least one group). The top 10 enriched terms per subset were reported.

10. **Preranked gene-set enrichment analysis (GSEA).** Preranked GSEA was performed using the complete Wilcoxon-ranked gene lists (ranking statistic: wilcoxon_z) for each major class. Parameters: minimum gene set size 15, maximum 500, 1,000 permutations, seed 42, FDR threshold 0.05. Signed Normalized Enrichment Scores (NES) and FDR q-values were reported.

11. **Cross-cell-type synthesis.** Genes meeting the |log₂FC| ≥ 0.25 criterion in each major class were aggregated. A consensus ranking metric (|log₂FC| × fraction of groups in which the gene was expressed in the same direction) was computed to identify pan-retinal signatures.

# Transcriptional and Compositional Changes in DDX41 Mutant Retina: A Descriptive Single-Cell RNA-seq Analysis

## Abstract

We performed a descriptive, exploratory analysis of single-cell RNA-seq data comparing DDX41 mutant and wild-type (WT) retina. The dataset comprises 15,307 cells (9,047 WT; 6,260 DDX41) spanning 11 major retinal cell classes. Because only one library exists per condition, all findings are reported as descriptive effect-size rankings rather than inferential differential expression. Five of eleven major classes (AC, BC, Cone, MG, Rod) met minimum cell-count thresholds for stratified analysis; six classes (Endothelial, HC, Microglia, Pericyte, RGC, RPE) were excluded due to insufficient cell numbers. The DDX41 mutant retina shows a clear reorganization: Müller Glia (MG) and Amacrine (AC) cell proportions expand (2.13× and 2.20×, respectively), while Bipolar (BC) and Cone proportions contract (0.68× and 0.32×). At the transcriptional level, a pan-retinal up-regulation of translation-related genes is observed across all five tested classes, while phototransduction pathways are down-regulated in AC, BC, and Rod. MG shows the strongest reactive gliosis signal (Gfap, log₂FC = +6.02), and Rods exhibit the most extreme single-gene change (Col25a1, log₂FC = +8.74). These findings are hypotheses to be validated with replicated experiments.

---

## 1. Methods

### 1.1 Data and Quality Control

The dataset is a processed single-cell RNA-seq AnnData object (`.h5ad`) containing 15,307 cells and 33,696 genes. Cells were filtered using pre-computed quality metrics: minimum 200 detected genes, maximum 10% mitochondrial reads, and singlet classification only (all 15,307 cells were classified as singlets). Genes detected in fewer than 3 cells were removed, yielding 22,387 genes. Counts were log1p-transformed for downstream analysis. The top 2,000 highly variable genes were retained for dimensionality reduction. All analyses were executed in HPC SLURM mode.

### 1.2 Stratified Effect-Size Ranking

Because the dataset contains a single library per condition (WT: 1 donor; DDX41: 1 donor), no valid statistical test for replicability exists. We therefore performed a descriptive, exploratory ranking of effect sizes using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test (tie-corrected) comparing DDX41 cells against WT cells within each major class. Parameters: minimum detection in 10% of one population (`min_pct = 0.1`), minimum absolute log₂ fold-change of 0.25 (`lfc = 0.25`), no FDR cutoff applied (`padj = 1.0`). The top 50 genes per direction per group were extracted for reporting. Wilcoxon scores and log₂FC values are reported strictly as descriptive rank metrics, not as inferential differential expression.

### 1.3 Cell Composition

The fraction of cells belonging to each major class was calculated per condition. Because only one library exists per condition, proportions are reported descriptively without statistical testing.

### 1.4 Clustering

Cells were projected onto a 2-dimensional UMAP and grouped using Leiden clustering. The optimal resolution was selected by bootstrap stability (10 bootstraps, minimum stability threshold 0.9), yielding resolution = 0.2 with 20 clusters (stability = 0.9605). Principal components (n = 30) and neighborhood graph (15 neighbors) were used. Existing cell-type annotations (`majorclass`, `celltype`) were retained as the primary labels; de-novo cluster IDs were computed for visualization only.

### 1.5 Pathway Over-Representation Analysis (ORA)

Genes passing the log₂FC ≥ 0.25 threshold per major class and direction were tested for over-representation against three local pathway libraries: GO Biological Process 2023 (5,407 terms), Reactome 2022 (1,818 terms), and MSigDB Hallmark 2020 (50 terms). The background was the tested universe of 11,293 genes measured in this retina. A false discovery rate threshold of 0.05 was applied.

### 1.6 Preranked Gene-Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA)

The complete Wilcoxon-ranked gene lists per major class were walked against the same three pathway libraries using preranked GSEA. Parameters: minimum gene set size 15, maximum 500, 1,000 permutations, seed 42, FDR threshold 0.05, ranking statistic = Wilcoxon z-score. Signed Normalized Enrichment Scores (NES) indicate direction of coordinated pathway shift.

### 1.7 Cross-Cell-Type Synthesis

Per-class DE tables were aggregated to identify genes changing in the same direction across multiple major classes. A consensus ranking metric (|log₂FC| × fraction of groups in which the gene was expressed) was computed to prioritize robust pan-retinal changes.

---

## 2. Results

### 2.1 Data Overview and Quality Control

| Metric | Value |

| Total cells (input) | 15,307 |
| Total cells (after QC) | 15,307 (0% removed) |
| Genes (input) | 33,696 |
| Genes (after filtering) | 22,387 |
| Highly variable genes retained | 2,000 |
| Mitochondrial genes | 13 |
| WT cells | 9,047 |
| DDX41 cells | 6,260 |
| Major classes | 11 |
| Cell types | 87 |

No cells were removed by QC filters, indicating the dataset was pre-filtered. The DDX41 arm shows higher mean detected genes per cell (2,076 vs. 1,505 in WT), consistent with a more transcriptionally active or stressed population.

### 2.2 Cell Composition Shifts

The relative abundance of major retinal classes shifts substantially between conditions (descriptive only; no statistical test):

| Major Class | WT (%) | DDX41 (%) | Fold (D/W) | Absolute Change (pp) |
|-------------|--------|-----------|------------|----------------------|
| Rod | 66.02 | 65.24 | 0.99 | −0.78 |
| BC | 18.88 | 12.80 | 0.68 | −6.08 |
| MG | 5.91 | 12.57 | 2.13 | +6.66 |
| Cone | 5.52 | 1.79 | 0.32 | −3.73 |
| AC | 2.85 | 6.26 | 2.20 | +3.41 |

| Pericyte | 0.02 | 0.06 | 2.91 | +0.04 |
| RPE | 0.02 | 0.03 | 1.45 | +0.01 |

The most notable shifts are: (i) MG more than doubles in proportion (5.91% → 12.57%), representing the largest absolute gain; (ii) AC also doubles (2.85% → 6.26%); (iii) BC loses the largest absolute proportion (−6.08 pp); and (iv) Cone is depleted ~3-fold (5.52% → 1.79%). Rod proportion remains essentially stable (66.02% → 65.24%).

### 2.3 Stratified Expression Changes

**Coverage:** 5 of 11 major classes were tested. Six classes were **not covered** because fewer than 30 cells were present in one or both arms:

| Excluded Class | WT cells | DDX41 cells | Reason |
|----------------|----------|-------------|--------|
| Endothelial | 7 | 27 | DDX41 arm < 30 |

| RGC | 6 | 8 | Both arms < 30 |

No findings are reported for these six classes.

|-------|-------------|---------------------|------------------------|----------------------|------------------------|
| AC | 8,371 | 2,462 | 1,509 | Angpt1 (+2.58) | Apoe (−4.91) |
| BC | 7,309 | 1,810 | 524 | Xlr3b (+3.83) | Sorcs3 (−2.19) |
| Cone | 6,840 | 2,800 | 1,102 | Cartpt (+5.99) | Kcne2 (−2.11) |
| MG | 9,720 | 5,057 | 987 | Gfap (+6.02) | Grin2b (−3.46) |
| Rod | 4,649 | 3,283 | 132 | Col25a1 (+8.74) | Dcc (−5.83) |

**AC (Amacrine):** Up-regulated genes are dominated by ribosomal and proteasomal components (Ubb, H3f3b, Rpl/Rps family), consistent with a translational stress response. Down-regulated genes include phototransduction cascade members (Apoe −4.91, Pde6g −1.90, Rho −1.84, Gnat1 −1.68), which is notable given that ACs are non-photoreceptor interneurons, suggesting a secondary signaling effect from photoreceptor dysfunction.

**BC (Bipolar):** Strong up-regulation of immune/inflammatory genes (Xlr3b +3.83, A2m +3.32, C4b/Serping1 family) and immediate-early response genes (Fos +2.35, Egr1 +2.48, Junb +1.98) indicates acute transcriptional activation. Down-regulated genes include phototransduction components.

**Cone:** Cones are overwhelmingly up-regulated (2,800 up vs. 1,102 down genes passing threshold). The strongest signal is Cartpt (log₂FC +5.99). Down-regulated genes include ion channels (Kcne2, Kcnma1) and metabolic genes. The pattern suggests a compensatory or survival transcriptional programme rather than simple degeneration.

**MG (Müller Glia):** The strongest up-regulated gene is Gfap (log₂FC +6.02), a canonical marker of reactive gliosis. Immune genes are also strongly up-regulated (C4b +3.26, Serping1 +2.90, A2m +1.70). Down-regulated genes include synaptic receptors (Grin2b −3.46, Grin2d −3.18), consistent with synaptic remodeling.

**Rod:** The most extreme single-gene change in the entire dataset is Col25a1 (log₂FC +8.74), an extracellular matrix/injury-response gene. Other up-regulated genes include Fgf2os (+2.57) and Fgf2 (+2.46). Down-regulated genes include axon guidance and synaptic genes (Dcc −5.83, Nrn1 −5.35, Aplp2 −4.91). The pattern suggests a dramatic extracellular matrix/fibrotic response in addition to phototransduction loss.

### 2.4 Pathway Enrichment — Over-Representation Analysis

ORA was performed on genes passing |log₂FC| ≥ 0.25 per class and direction, against the tested universe of 11,293 genes.

**Up-regulated pathways:**

| AC | Cytoplasmic Translation (GO:0002181); Eukaryotic Translation Elongation R-HSA-156842; Peptide Chain Elongation R-HSA-156902; Viral mRNA Translation R-HSA-192823; Selenocysteine Synthesis R-HSA-2408557 |

**Down-regulated pathways:**

|-------|---------------------------|
| AC | Activation Of Phototransduction Cascade R-HSA-2485179; Visual Phototransduction R-HSA-2187338; Phototransduction Cascade R-HSA-2514856; Sensory Perception R-HSA-9709957; Inactivation, Recovery And Regulation Of Phototransduction Cascade R-HSA-2514859 |
| BC | Phototransduction Cascade R-HSA-2514856; Inactivation, Recovery And Regulation Of Phototransduction Cascade R-HSA-2514859; Activation Of Phototransduction Cascade R-HSA-2485179; Visual Phototransduction R-HSA-2187338; Homophilic Cell Adhesion Via Plasma Membrane Adhesion Molecules (GO:0007156) |

### 2.5 Pathway Enrichment — Preranked GSEA

Preranked GSEA was applied to the full Wilcoxon-ranked lists per class. Significant terms (FDR < 0.05):

|-------|-------------------|----|------|----------------------|------------------------|

The strongest down-regulated pathway in the entire dataset is Visual Phototransduction in Rods (NES = −4.25, FDR = 0.0). Cone shows a strikingly asymmetric pattern: 24 down-regulated pathways (dominated by glycolysis, pyruvate metabolism, and hypoxia) versus only 1 up-regulated pathway.

### 2.6 Cross-Cell-Type Consensus

The pan-retinal up-regulation of ribosomal proteins (Rps20), mitochondrial genes (mt-Cytb), and translational machinery genes (Ubb, Hmgn2) across all five tested classes supports a global translational activation response to DDX41 loss.

### 2.7 Clustering

Leiden clustering at resolution 0.2 (selected by bootstrap stability = 0.9605) yielded 20 clusters. The two largest clusters (0: 6,199 cells; 1: 3,738 cells) correspond to the dominant Rod population. Existing `majorclass` and `celltype` annotations were used as the primary biological labels throughout this report; de-novo cluster IDs are not biologically interpretable and were used only for visualization.

---

## 3. Discussion

The DDX41 mutant retina exhibits a coordinated, multi-cellular transcriptional response that can be summarized in three interlocking themes:

**1. Global translational activation.** The most consistent finding across all five tested cell classes is up-regulation of translation-related pathways (Cytoplasmic Translation, Eukaryotic Translation Elongation, Peptide Chain Elongation, Translation). This is detected by both ORA and preranked GSEA, and is supported by the cross-class consensus showing ribosomal and mitochondrial genes (Ubb, Rps20, mt-Cytb, Hmgn2) up-regulated in 4–5 of 5 classes. Given that DDX41 is an RNA helicase involved in transcription and splicing, a compensatory up-regulation of translational capacity is a plausible mechanistic consequence, though this remains a hypothesis requiring validation.

**2. Phototransduction loss with secondary effects.** Phototransduction pathways (Visual Phototransduction, Phototransduction Cascade, Activation of Phototransduction Cascade) are down-regulated in Rods (NES = −4.25, the strongest signal in the dataset), BCs, and ACs. The presence of phototransduction gene down-regulation in non-photoreceptor cells (AC, BC) suggests that the loss is not confined to photoreceptors but propagates to neighboring interneurons, possibly through altered synaptic signaling or paracrine factors.

**3. Reactive gliosis and inflammatory activation.** MG shows the strongest single-gene up-regulation (Gfap, log₂FC = +6.02) and the largest proportional expansion (5.91% → 12.57%). Complement components (C4b, Serping1, A2m) are up-regulated in both MG and BC, indicating a neuroinflammatory response. The down-regulation of synaptic and adhesion pathways in MG (Nervous System Development, Cell-Cell Adhesion, Axon Guidance, Synapse Assembly) is consistent with a shift from a homeostatic to a reactive glial state.

**4. Metabolic reprogramming in Cones and Rods.** Cone cells show a striking down-regulation of glycolytic and pyruvate metabolic pathways (Glycolytic Process, Pyruvate Metabolic Process, Hypoxia, Glycolysis) while up-regulating Oxidative Phosphorylation. Rods show a similar metabolic shift (Hypoxia and Glycolytic Process down) combined with up-regulation of mitochondrial electron transport. This suggests a metabolic switch from glycolysis toward oxidative phosphorylation in photoreceptors, which may reflect either a compensatory adaptation or early metabolic stress.

**5. Extracellular matrix and injury response in Rods.** The extreme up-regulation of Col25a1 (log₂FC = +8.74) and Fgf2/Fgf2os in Rods, combined with down-regulation of axon guidance genes (Dcc, Nrn1, Aplp2), suggests that rods undergo a structural remodeling or fibrotic response in addition to phototransduction loss.

---

## 4. Limitations

1. **Single library per condition.** The most critical limitation is the absence of biological replicates. All expression comparisons, composition shifts, and pathway enrichments are descriptive and exploratory. No p-values or FDR values should be interpreted as evidence of statistical significance in the inferential sense. The Wilcoxon scores and log₂FC values are rank metrics and effect sizes, respectively.

2. **Six cell classes not analyzed.** Endothelial, HC, Microglia, Pericyte, RGC, and RPE were excluded from stratified DE because fewer than 30 cells were present in one or both arms. These classes may harbor important disease-relevant changes (e.g., Microglia expansion is evident in composition data) but cannot be characterized at the single-gene level with the current data.

3. **No batch correction or integration.** With one library per condition, batch effects are confounded with the condition effect. Any technical differences between the two libraries would be indistinguishable from biological signal.

4. **Pre-existing annotations.** Cell-type labels were inherited from the input dataset (scANVI-based semi-supervised annotation). No independent validation of annotation accuracy was performed in this analysis.

5. **Enrichment is association, not causation.** Pathway enrichment identifies gene sets whose members are collectively shifted; it does not establish pathway activity, direction of causation, or functional consequence.

---

## 5. Conclusions

The DDX41 mutant retina displays a multi-cellular transcriptional reorganization characterized by: (i) a pan-retinal up-regulation of translational machinery; (ii) loss of phototransduction in photoreceptors and secondary interneurons; (iii) reactive Müller gliosis with neuroinflammatory activation; (iv) metabolic reprogramming in photoreceptors toward oxidative phosphorylation; and (v) extracellular matrix remodeling in Rods. Cell composition shifts (MG and AC expansion; BC and Cone contraction) are consistent with these transcriptional changes. All findings are descriptive hypotheses that require validation with replicated experiments, orthogonal assays (e.g., RNA FISH, proteomics), and functional studies to establish causality and temporal dynamics.

# Pan-retinal translational activation and phototransduction loss characterize the DDX41 mutant retina

## Abstract

We performed a descriptive, exploratory single-cell RNA-seq analysis comparing DDX41 mutant and wild-type (WT) retina, comprising 15,307 cells (9,047 WT; 6,260 DDX41) spanning 11 major retinal cell classes. Because only one library exists per condition, all findings are reported as descriptive effect-size rankings rather than inferential differential expression. The DDX41 mutant retina shows a clear compositional reorganization: Müller Glia and Amacrine cell proportions expand (2.13× and 2.20×, respectively), while Bipolar and Cone proportions contract (0.68× and 0.32×). At the transcriptional level, a pan-retinal up-regulation of translation-related genes is observed across all five tested classes, while phototransduction pathways are down-regulated in Amacrine, Bipolar, and Rod cells. Müller Glia shows the strongest reactive gliosis signal (*Gfap*, log₂FC = +6.02), and Rods exhibit the most extreme single-gene change (*Col25a1*, log₂FC = +8.74). These findings constitute a set of hypotheses to be validated with replicated experiments.

## What was run

Each analysis below was performed by the named tool. Settings are given with what they do; a value marked **chosen for this run** was not the tool's default.

**1. `run_scanpy_qc`** — Measured each cell's quality (how many genes it detects, how much of its signal is mitochondrial), discarded the cells and genes that fall below the thresholds below, and normalised the remaining counts so later comparisons reflect biology rather than sequencing depth.

    - `min_genes` = `200` — drop a cell detecting fewer genes than this — an empty droplet or a dying cell
    - `min_cells` = `3` — drop a gene detected in fewer cells than this — too sparse to support any test
    - `max_pct_mt` = `10` — drop a cell whose reads are more than this percent mitochondrial (a stressed or lysed cell). 10 is the common working threshold for tissue; the Seurat and scanpy tutorials use 5 for PBMC, and single NUCLEI need far less (1-5) because a nucleus should carry almost no mitochondrial signal. Raise it only for a tissue known to be mitochondria-rich, and say so
    - `n_top_genes` = `2000` — how many highly-variable genes to keep for the embedding — more genes carry more structure and more noise. 2000 is Seurat's default and the usual starting point

**2. `run_code`** — Ran a purpose-written analysis script in the sandbox for a step no packaged tool covers.

**3. `run_de`** — Tested, gene by gene, whether expression differs between the groups being compared, using a Wilcoxon rank-sum test over individual cells. In marker mode each group is compared with all remaining cells; given a reference level it compares one condition against a control, and given a cell-type column it repeats that comparison separately within each cell type.

    - `groupby` = `sampleid` — the obs column whose levels are compared — **chosen for this run**
    - `reference` = `WT` — the baseline level. 'rest' gives one-vs-rest MARKERS; a named level (e.g. 'WT') gives a real condition-vs-control contrast — **chosen for this run**
    - `stratify_by` = `majorclass` — an EXISTING cell-type column — runs the contrast separately within each cell type instead of pooling them — **chosen for this run**
    - `n_genes` = `50` — rows kept per group — per DIRECTION when it is a contrast
    - `min_pct` = `0.1` — a gene must be detected in at least this fraction of the cells of one of the two populations compared, or it is not tested at all (Seurat FindMarkers' min.pct). Without it most genes enter the test undetected — on the DDX41 retina object 2/3 did — which triples the BH denominator and floods the ranking with divide-by-zero fold-changes above 2^20. 0 disables
    - `lfc` = `0.25` — minimum |log2 fold-change| for calling a gene significant — applied together with `padj`, and drawn as the volcano's vertical line. 0.25 is the single-cell convention (Seurat's FindMarkers threshold); 1.0 is a bulk-RNA habit and hides most real single-cell effects
    - `padj` = `1` — adjusted-p (Benjamini-Hochberg) cutoff for calling a gene significant — **chosen for this run**

**4. `run_composition`** — Counted what fraction of each arm's cells belongs to each cell type, and compared those proportions between the arms — whether a population expanded or shrank, as opposed to whether its genes changed.

    - `select_resolution` = `True` — choose the resolution by bootstrap stability instead of accepting the default — **chosen for this run**

## Study question

This analysis asks what transcriptional and compositional changes distinguish DDX41 mutant retina from wild-type retina at single-cell resolution. The question is answerable from this dataset because it contains 15,307 cells spanning 11 major retinal classes across both conditions, with sufficient cell numbers in five classes to permit stratified effect-size comparisons. Because the dataset contains a single library per condition, the analysis is necessarily descriptive and exploratory, yielding ranked effect sizes and pathway associations rather than inferential differential expression.

## Results

### Quality control

The input dataset contained 15,307 cells and 33,696 genes. After applying quality filters (minimum 200 detected genes per cell, maximum 10% mitochondrial reads, singlet classification only) and removing genes detected in fewer than 3 cells, all 15,307 cells were retained (0% removed) and 22,387 genes remained. The DDX41 arm showed a higher mean number of detected genes per cell (2,076) compared to WT (1,505), consistent with a more transcriptionally active or stressed population. The top 2,000 highly variable genes were retained for downstream dimensionality reduction.

### Cell composition

The relative abundance of major retinal classes shifts substantially between conditions. The most notable changes are: (i) Müller Glia more than doubles in proportion (5.91% → 12.57%, fold 2.13), representing the largest absolute gain (+6.66 percentage points); (ii) Amacrine cells also double (2.85% → 6.26%, fold 2.20); (iii) Bipolar cells lose the largest absolute proportion (−6.08 pp, fold 0.68); and (iv) Cone cells are depleted approximately 3-fold (5.52% → 1.79%, fold 0.32). Rod proportion remains essentially stable (66.02% → 65.24%, fold 0.99). Microglia show a 3.62-fold increase in proportion (0.27% → 0.96%), though the absolute change is small (+0.69 pp).

### Cell clustering

Leiden clustering at resolution 0.2 (selected by bootstrap stability = 0.9605) yielded 20 clusters. The two largest clusters (cluster 0: 6,199 cells; cluster 1: 3,738 cells) correspond to the dominant Rod population. Existing cell-type annotations were retained as the primary biological labels; de-novo cluster IDs were used only for visualization.

### Differential expression (descriptive effect-size ranking)

Five of eleven major classes were tested for stratified expression changes. Six classes (Endothelial, Horizontal Cell, Microglia, Pericyte, Retinal Ganglion Cell, Retinal Pigment Epithelium) were excluded because fewer than 30 cells were present in one or both arms.

Across the five tested classes, the following patterns emerged:

**Amacrine cells** (8,371 genes tested; 2,462 up, 1,509 down passing threshold). Up-regulated genes are dominated by ribosomal and proteasomal components (*Ubb*, *H3f3b*, *Rpl/Rps* family), consistent with a translational stress response. Down-regulated genes include phototransduction cascade members (*Apoe* −4.91, *Pde6g* −1.90, *Rho* −1.84, *Gnat1* −1.68), which is notable given that Amacrine cells are non-photoreceptor interneurons, suggesting a secondary signaling effect from photoreceptor dysfunction.

**Bipolar cells** (7,309 genes tested; 1,810 up, 524 down). Strong up-regulation of immune/inflammatory genes (*Xlr3b* +3.83, *A2m* +3.32, *C4b*/*Serping1* family) and immediate-early response genes (*Fos* +2.35, *Egr1* +2.48, *Junb* +1.98) indicates acute transcriptional activation. Down-regulated genes include phototransduction components.

**Cone cells** (6,840 genes tested; 2,800 up, 1,102 down). Cones are overwhelmingly up-regulated. The strongest signal is *Cartpt* (log₂FC +5.99). Down-regulated genes include ion channels (*Kcne2*, *Kcnma1*) and metabolic genes. The pattern suggests a compensatory or survival transcriptional programme rather than simple degeneration.

**Müller Glia** (9,720 genes tested; 5,057 up, 987 down). The strongest up-regulated gene is *Gfap* (log₂FC +6.02), a canonical marker of reactive gliosis. Immune genes are also strongly up-regulated (*C4b* +3.26, *Serping1* +2.90, *A2m* +1.70). Down-regulated genes include synaptic receptors (*Grin2b* −3.46, *Grin2d* −3.18), consistent with synaptic remodeling.

**Rod cells** (4,649 genes tested; 3,283 up, 132 down). The most extreme single-gene change in the entire dataset is *Col25a1* (log₂FC +8.74), an extracellular matrix/injury-response gene. Other up-regulated genes include *Fgf2os* (+2.57) and *Fgf2* (+2.46). Down-regulated genes include axon guidance and synaptic genes (*Dcc* −5.83, *Nrn1* −5.35, *Aplp2* −4.91). Cone down-regulated pathways are dominated by glycolysis and carbohydrate metabolism (Glycolytic Process GO:0006096, Carbohydrate Catabolic Process GO:0016052, Pyruvate Metabolic Process GO:0006090, Hypoxia). Müller Glia down-regulated pathways include Nervous System Development (GO:0007399), Cell-Cell Adhesion (GO:0098742), Axon Guidance (GO:0007411), and Synapse Assembly (GO:0007416). ### Cross-cell-type consensus

Aggregation of expression tables across all five tested classes identified 1,715 genes up-regulated in the same direction in at least one class. The top consensus up-regulated genes include *Hmgn2* (up in 5/5 classes, max |log₂FC| 1.61, consensus score 0.664), *Ubb* (5/5, max |log₂FC| 1.05, score 0.660), *mt-Cytb* (4/5, max |log₂FC| 2.07, score 0.575), *Rps20* (5/5, max |log₂FC| 1.32, score 0.486), and *Klhl29* (4/5, max |log₂FC| 3.24). The pan-retinal up-regulation of ribosomal proteins, mitochondrial genes, and translational machinery genes across all five tested classes supports a global translational activation response to DDX41 loss.

## Discussion

The DDX41 mutant retina exhibits a coordinated, multi-cellular transcriptional response that can be summarized in five interlocking themes.

First, a global translational activation is the most consistent finding across all five tested cell classes. Translation-related pathways (Cytoplasmic Translation, Eukaryotic Translation Elongation, Peptide Chain Elongation, Translation) are up-regulated in every class, detected by both over-representation analysis and preranked GSEA, and supported by the cross-class consensus showing ribosomal and mitochondrial genes (*Ubb*, *Rps20*, *mt-Cytb*, *Hmgn2*) up-regulated in 4–5 of 5 classes. Given that DDX41 is an RNA helicase involved in transcription and splicing, a compensatory up-regulation of translational capacity is a plausible mechanistic consequence, though this remains a hypothesis requiring validation.

Second, phototransduction loss extends beyond photoreceptors. Phototransduction pathways are down-regulated in Rods (NES = −4.25, the strongest signal in the dataset), Bipolar cells, and Amacrine cells. The presence of phototransduction gene down-regulation in non-photoreceptor interneurons suggests that the loss propagates to neighboring cells, possibly through altered synaptic signaling or paracrine factors.

Third, reactive gliosis and neuroinflammatory activation are prominent. Müller Glia shows the strongest single-gene up-regulation (*Gfap*, log₂FC = +6.02) and the largest proportional expansion (5.91% → 12.57%). Complement components (*C4b*, *Serping1*, *A2m*) are up-regulated in both Müller Glia and Bipolar cells. The down-regulation of synaptic and adhesion pathways in Müller Glia (Nervous System Development, Cell-Cell Adhesion, Axon Guidance, Synapse Assembly) is consistent with a shift from a homeostatic to a reactive glial state.

Fourth, metabolic reprogramming in photoreceptors is evident. Cone cells show a striking down-regulation of glycolytic and pyruvate metabolic pathways while up-regulating Oxidative Phosphorylation. Rods show a similar metabolic shift (Hypoxia and Glycolytic Process down) combined with up-regulation of mitochondrial electron transport (GO:0006120, NES = +2.44). This suggests a metabolic switch from glycolysis toward oxidative phosphorylation, which may reflect either a compensatory adaptation or early metabolic stress.

Fifth, extracellular matrix and injury response in Rods is marked by the extreme up-regulation of *Col25a1* (log₂FC = +8.74) and *Fgf2*/*Fgf2os*, combined with down-regulation of axon guidance genes (*Dcc*, *Nrn1*, *Aplp2*), suggesting structural remodeling or fibrotic response in addition to phototransduction loss.

## Limitations

- **Single library per condition.** The absence of biological replicates means all expression comparisons, composition shifts, and pathway enrichments are descriptive and exploratory. No p-values or FDR values should be interpreted as evidence of statistical significance in the inferential sense. The Wilcoxon scores and log₂FC values are rank metrics and effect sizes, respectively.
- **Six cell classes not analyzed.** Endothelial, Horizontal Cell, Microglia, Pericyte, Retinal Ganglion Cell, and Retinal Pigment Epithelium were excluded from stratified analysis because fewer than 30 cells were present in one or both arms. These classes may harbor important disease-relevant changes (e.g., Microglia expansion is evident in composition data) but cannot be characterized at the single-gene level with the current data.
- **No batch correction or integration.** With one library per condition, batch effects are confounded with the condition effect. Any technical differences between the two libraries would be indistinguishable from biological signal.
- **Pre-existing annotations.** Cell-type labels were inherited from the input dataset (scANVI-based semi-supervised annotation). No independent validation of annotation accuracy was performed in this analysis.
- **Enrichment is association, not causation.** Pathway enrichment identifies gene sets whose members are collectively shifted; it does not establish pathway activity, direction of causation, or functional consequence.

## Conclusion

We performed a descriptive single-cell RNA-seq analysis of DDX41 mutant versus wild-type retina and identified a multi-cellular transcriptional reorganization characterized by pan-retinal translational activation, phototransduction loss in photoreceptors and secondary interneurons, reactive Müller gliosis with neuroinflammatory activation, metabolic reprogramming toward oxidative phosphorylation in photoreceptors, and extracellular matrix remodeling in Rods. Cell composition shifts (Müller Glia and Amacrine expansion; Bipolar and Cone contraction) are consistent with these transcriptional changes. All findings are descriptive hypotheses that require validation with replicated experiments, orthogonal assays, and functional studies to establish causality and temporal dynamics.

## Methods

1. **Dataset.** A processed single-cell RNA-seq AnnData object (`.h5ad`) containing 15,307 cells and 33,696 genes was used. Cells were partitioned into 9,047 WT and 6,260 DDX41 mutant cells, spanning 11 major retinal classes and 87 fine-grained cell types. All analyses were executed in HPC SLURM mode.

2. **Quality control.** Cells were filtered using pre-computed quality metrics: minimum 200 detected genes per cell, maximum 10% mitochondrial reads, and singlet classification only. All 15,307 cells were classified as singlets and passed all filters (0% removed). Genes detected in fewer than 3 cells were removed, yielding 22,387 genes. Counts were log1p-transformed for downstream analysis.

3. **Highly variable gene selection.** The top 2,000 highly variable genes were retained for dimensionality reduction.

4. **Dimensionality reduction.** Principal component analysis was performed with n_comps = 30.

5. **Neighborhood graph construction.** A k-nearest neighbor graph was constructed with n_neighbors = 15.

6. **Clustering.** Leiden clustering was applied. The optimal resolution was selected by bootstrap stability (10 bootstraps, minimum stability threshold 0.9), yielding resolution = 0.2 with 20 clusters (stability = 0.9605). Existing cell-type annotations (`majorclass`, `celltype`) were retained as the primary biological labels; de-novo cluster IDs were computed for visualization only.

7. **UMAP embedding.** Cells were projected onto a 2-dimensional UMAP for visualization.

8. **Stratified effect-size ranking.** Because the dataset contains a single library per condition, no valid statistical test for replicability exists. A descriptive, exploratory ranking of effect sizes was performed using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test (tie-corrected) comparing DDX41 cells against WT cells within each major class. Parameters: minimum detection in 10% of one population (`min_pct = 0.1`), minimum absolute log₂ fold-change of 0.25 (`lfc = 0.25`), no FDR cutoff applied (`padj = 1.0`). The top 50 genes per direction per group were extracted for reporting. Wilcoxon scores and log₂FC values are reported strictly as descriptive rank metrics, not as inferential differential expression. Five of eleven major classes (Amacrine, Bipolar, Cone, Müller Glia, Rod) met the minimum cell-count threshold (≥30 cells in both arms) for stratified analysis; six classes (Endothelial, Horizontal Cell, Microglia, Pericyte, Retinal Ganglion Cell, Retinal Pigment Epithelium) were excluded.

9. **Cell composition.** The fraction of cells belonging to each major class was calculated per condition. Proportions are reported descriptively without statistical testing.

10. **Over-representation analysis (ORA).** Genes passing the log₂FC ≥ 0.25 threshold per major class and direction were tested for over-representation against three local pathway libraries: GO Biological Process 2023 (5,407 terms), Reactome 2022 (1,818 terms), and MSigDB Hallmark 2020 (50 terms). The background was the tested universe of 11,293 genes measured in this retina. A false discovery rate threshold of 0.05 was applied.

11. **Preranked gene-set enrichment analysis (GSEA).** The complete Wilcoxon-ranked gene lists per major class were walked against the same three pathway libraries using preranked GSEA. Parameters: minimum gene set size 15, maximum 500, 1,000 permutations, seed 42, FDR threshold 0.05, ranking statistic = Wilcoxon z-score. Signed Normalized Enrichment Scores (NES) indicate direction of coordinated pathway shift.

12. **Cross-cell-type synthesis.** Per-class DE tables were aggregated to identify genes changing in the same direction across multiple major classes. A consensus ranking metric (|log₂FC| × fraction of groups in which the gene was expressed) was computed to prioritize robust pan-retinal changes.

The DDX41 mutant retina exhibits a coordinated, multi-cellular transcriptional response that can be summarized in five interlocking themes.

First, a global translational activation is the most consistent finding across all five tested cell classes. Translation-related pathways (Cytoplasmic Translation, Eukaryotic Translation Elongation, Peptide Chain Elongation, Translation) are up-regulated in every class, detected by both over-representation analysis and preranked GSEA, and supported by the cross-class consensus showing ribosomal and mitochondrial genes (*Ubb*, *Rps20*, *mt-Cytb*, *Hmgn2*) up-regulated in 4–5 of 5 classes. Given that DDX41 is an RNA helicase involved in transcription and splicing, a compensatory up-regulation of translational capacity is a plausible mechanistic consequence, though this remains a hypothesis requiring validation.

Second, phototransduction loss extends beyond photoreceptors. Phototransduction pathways are down-regulated in Rods (NES = −4.25, the strongest signal in the dataset), Bipolar cells, and Amacrine cells. The presence of phototransduction gene down-regulation in non-photoreceptor interneurons suggests that the loss propagates to neighboring cells, possibly through altered synaptic signaling or paracrine factors.

Third, reactive gliosis and neuroinflammatory activation are prominent. Müller Glia shows the strongest single-gene up-regulation (*Gfap*, log₂FC = +6.02) and the largest proportional expansion (5.91% → 12.57%). Complement components (*C4b*, *Serping1*, *A2m*) are up-regulated in both Müller Glia and Bipolar cells. The down-regulation of synaptic and adhesion pathways in Müller Glia (Nervous System Development, Cell-Cell Adhesion, Axon Guidance, Synapse Assembly) is consistent with a shift from a homeostatic to a reactive glial state.

Fourth, metabolic reprogramming in photoreceptors is evident. Cone cells show a striking down-regulation of glycolytic and pyruvate metabolic pathways while up-regulating Oxidative Phosphorylation. Rods show a similar metabolic shift (Hypoxia and Glycolytic Process down) combined with up-regulation of mitochondrial electron transport (GO:0006120, NES = +2.44). This suggests a metabolic switch from glycolysis toward oxidative phosphorylation, which may reflect either a compensatory adaptation or early metabolic stress.

Fifth, extracellular matrix and injury response in Rods is marked by the extreme up-regulation of *Col25a1* (log₂FC = +8.74) and *Fgf2*/*Fgf2os*, combined with down-regulation of axon guidance genes (*Dcc*, *Nrn1*, *Aplp2*), suggesting structural remodeling or fibrotic response in addition to phototransduction loss.

## Limitations

- **Single library per condition.** The absence of biological replicates means all expression comparisons, composition shifts, and pathway enrichments are descriptive and exploratory. No p-values or FDR values should be interpreted as evidence of statistical significance in the inferential sense. The Wilcoxon scores and log₂FC values are rank metrics and effect sizes, respectively.
- **Six cell classes not analyzed.** Endothelial, Horizontal Cell, Microglia, Pericyte, Retinal Ganglion Cell, and Retinal Pigment Epithelium were excluded from stratified analysis because fewer than 30 cells were present in one or both arms. These classes may harbor important disease-relevant changes (e.g., Microglia expansion is evident in composition data) but cannot be characterized at the single-gene level with the current data.
- **No batch correction or integration.** With one library per condition, batch effects are confounded with the condition effect. Any technical differences between the two libraries would be indistinguishable from biological signal.
- **Pre-existing annotations.** Cell-type labels were inherited from the input dataset (scANVI-based semi-supervised annotation). No independent validation of annotation accuracy was performed in this analysis.
- **Enrichment is association, not causation.** Pathway enrichment identifies gene sets whose members are collectively shifted; it does not establish pathway activity, direction of causation, or functional consequence.

## Conclusion

We performed a descriptive single-cell RNA-seq analysis of DDX41 mutant versus wild-type retina and identified a multi-cellular transcriptional reorganization characterized by pan-retinal translational activation, phototransduction loss in photoreceptors and secondary interneurons, reactive Müller gliosis with neuroinflammatory activation, metabolic reprogramming toward oxidative phosphorylation in photoreceptors, and extracellular matrix remodeling in Rods. Cell composition shifts (Müller Glia and Amacrine expansion; Bipolar and Cone contraction) are consistent with these transcriptional changes. All findings are descriptive hypotheses that require validation with replicated experiments, orthogonal assays, and functional studies to establish causality and temporal dynamics.

## Methods

1. **Dataset.** A processed single-cell RNA-seq AnnData object (`.h5ad`) containing 15,307 cells and 33,696 genes was used. Cells were partitioned into 9,047 WT and 6,260 DDX41 mutant cells, spanning 11 major retinal classes and 87 fine-grained cell types. All analyses were executed in HPC SLURM mode.

2. **Quality control.** Cells were filtered using pre-computed quality metrics: minimum 200 detected genes per cell, maximum 10% mitochondrial reads, and singlet classification only. All 15,307 cells were classified as singlets and passed all filters (0% removed). Genes detected in fewer than 3 cells were removed, yielding 22,387 genes. Counts were log1p-transformed for downstream analysis.

3. **Highly variable gene selection.** The top 2,000 highly variable genes were retained for dimensionality reduction.

4. **Dimensionality reduction.** Principal component analysis was performed with n_comps = 30.

5. **Neighborhood graph construction.** A k-nearest neighbor graph was constructed with n_neighbors = 15.

6. **Clustering.** Leiden clustering was applied. The optimal resolution was selected by bootstrap stability (10 bootstraps, minimum stability threshold 0.9), yielding resolution = 0.2 with 20 clusters (stability = 0.9605). Existing cell-type annotations (`majorclass`, `celltype`) were retained as the primary biological labels; de-novo cluster IDs were computed for visualization only.

7. **UMAP embedding.** Cells were projected onto a 2-dimensional UMAP for visualization.

8. **Stratified effect-size ranking.** Because the dataset contains a single library per condition, no valid statistical test for replicability exists. A descriptive, exploratory ranking of effect sizes was performed using the Wilcoxon rank-sum test (tie-corrected) comparing DDX41 cells against WT cells within each major class. Parameters: minimum detection in 10% of one population (`min_pct = 0.1`), minimum absolute log₂ fold-change of 0.25 (`lfc = 0.25`), no FDR cutoff applied (`padj = 1.0`). The top 50 genes per direction per group were extracted for reporting. Wilcoxon scores and log₂FC values are reported strictly as descriptive rank metrics, not as inferential differential expression. Five of eleven major classes (Amacrine, Bipolar, Cone, Müller Glia, Rod) met the minimum cell-count threshold (≥30 cells in both arms) for stratified analysis; six classes (Endothelial, Horizontal Cell, Microglia, Pericyte, Retinal Ganglion Cell, Retinal Pigment Epithelium) were excluded.

9. **Cell composition.** The fraction of cells belonging to each major class was calculated per condition. Proportions are reported descriptively without statistical testing.

10. **Over-representation analysis (ORA).** Genes passing the log₂FC ≥ 0.25 threshold per major class and direction were tested for over-representation against three local pathway libraries: GO Biological Process 2023 (5,407 terms), Reactome 2022 (1,818 terms), and MSigDB Hallmark 2020 (50 terms). The background was the tested universe of 11,293 genes measured in this retina. A false discovery rate threshold of 0.05 was applied.

11. **Preranked gene-set enrichment analysis (GSEA).** The complete Wilcoxon-ranked gene lists per major class were walked against the same three pathway libraries using preranked GSEA. Parameters: minimum gene set size 15, maximum 500, 1,000 permutations, seed 42, FDR threshold 0.05, ranking statistic = Wilcoxon z-score. Signed Normalized Enrichment Scores (NES) indicate direction of coordinated pathway shift.

12. **Cross-cell-type synthesis.** Per-class DE tables were aggregated to identify genes changing in the same direction across multiple major classes. A consensus ranking metric (|log₂FC| × fraction of groups in which the gene was expressed) was computed to prioritize robust pan-retinal changes.

# Transcriptional and Compositional Changes in DDX41 Mutant vs. Wild-Type Retina: A Descriptive Single-Cell RNA-Seq Analysis

## Abstract

We performed a descriptive, exploratory analysis of a single-cell RNA-seq dataset comparing DDX41 mutant and wild-type (WT) mouse retina. The dataset contains 15,307 cells (9,047 WT; 6,260 DDX41) spanning 11 annotated retinal major classes. Because the data comprise a single library per condition (one donor each), all findings are reported as descriptive effect-size rankings rather than inferential differential expression. Five of eleven major classes (AC, BC, Cone, MG, Rod) met the minimum cell-count threshold for stratified analysis; six (Endothelial, HC, Microglia, Pericyte, RGC, RPE) were excluded. The DDX41 mutant retina shows a pronounced reorganization: Müller Glia (MG) and Amacrine (AC) cells expand in proportion while Bipolar (BC) and Cone cells contract. At the transcriptional level, a pan-retinal up-regulation of translation-related genes is observed across all five tested classes, while phototransduction pathways are strongly down-regulated in Rod, BC, and AC cells. MG cells mount a massive reactive gliosis programme (Gfap, log₂FC = +6.02), and Rod cells show extreme up-regulation of extracellular matrix and injury-response genes (Col25a1, log₂FC = +8.74). These findings are hypotheses to be validated with replicated experiments.

---

## 1. Introduction

DDX41 is an RNA helicase implicated in retinal degeneration. The present analysis characterizes the transcriptional and compositional landscape of the DDX41 mutant retina relative to WT at single-cell resolution. Because the dataset contains a single biological library per condition, the analysis is explicitly framed as descriptive and exploratory: effect sizes (log₂ fold-changes) and rank-based statistics are reported without inferential p-value interpretation.

---

## 2. Methods

### 2.1 Data and Quality Control

The input dataset (`Ddx41_DEG.h5ad`) is a processed single-cell RNA-seq AnnData object containing 15,307 cells and 33,696 genes. The dataset carries pre-computed UMAP coordinates, scVI latent embeddings (30-dimensional), scANVI prediction probabilities, and curated cell-type annotations (`celltype`, 87 categories; `majorclass`, 11 categories). The `sampleid` column encodes the DDX41 vs. WT contrast; `orig.ident` is a single level (0) for all cells, confirming one library per condition. All 15,307 cells are classified as Singlets.

Quality control filtering was applied using the following thresholds: minimum 200 genes per cell, maximum 10% mitochondrial reads, and singlet-only inclusion. No cells were removed (0.0% removal rate). Gene-level filtering retained genes detected in at least 3 cells, reducing the feature space from 33,696 to 22,387 genes. Counts were normalized and log1p-transformed. The top 2,000 highly variable genes were selected for downstream dimensional reduction.

### 2.2 Stratified Differential Expression (Effect Ranking)

Per-cell-type effect rankings were generated using a Wilcoxon rank-sum test (tie-corrected) comparing DDX41 mutant cells against WT cells *within the same major class*. Parameters: `min_pct = 0.1` (gene must be detected in ≥10% of one population), `lfc = 0.25` (minimum |log₂FC|), `padj = 1.0` (no FDR cutoff applied, as no valid multiple-testing correction is possible with a single library per condition). The top 50 genes per direction per group were retained for reporting. The tested universe comprised 11,293 genes (after `min_pct` filtering).

**Five of eleven major classes were tested** (≥30 cells in both arms): AC (469 WT / 181 DDX41), BC (1,197 / 1,312), Cone (310 / 301), MG (803 / 519), Rod (6,578 / 3,479). **Six classes were not analyzed** because they fell below the 30-cell minimum in one or both arms: Endothelial (7 WT / 27 DDX41), HC (5 / 11), Microglia (60 / 24), Pericyte (4 / 2), RGC (6 / 8), RPE (2 / 2). No findings are reported for these six classes.

### 2.3 Cell Composition Mapping

The relative abundance of each major class was computed per condition. Because only one library exists per condition, proportions are reported descriptively without statistical testing.

### 2.4 Clustering

Leiden clustering was performed on the top 30 principal components with 15 neighbors per cell. The resolution was selected by bootstrap stability (10 bootstraps, minimum stability 0.9), yielding resolution = 0.2 and 20 clusters. The existing `majorclass` and `celltype` annotations were retained as the primary biological labels; de-novo cluster IDs were computed for visualization only.

### 2.5 Pathway Enrichment

Two complementary enrichment approaches were applied to the per-class DE tables:

1. **Over-representation analysis (ORA):** Genes passing the |log₂FC| ≥ 0.25 threshold were tested against three local gene-set libraries (GO_Biological_Process_2023: 5,407 terms; Reactome_2022: 1,818 terms; MSigDB_Hallmark_2020: 50 terms) using the tested universe (11,293 genes) as background. The top 10 enriched terms per direction per class were reported.

2. **Preranked gene-set enrichment analysis (GSEA):** The complete Wilcoxon-ranked gene lists (z-scores) for each major class were walked against the same three libraries. Parameters: minimum gene-set size 15, maximum 500, 1,000 permutations, FDR threshold 0.05. Signed Normalized Enrichment Scores (NES) and FDR q-values were reported.

### 2.6 Cross-Cell-Type Synthesis

Genes meeting the |log₂FC| ≥ 0.25 criterion in each class were aggregated. A consensus ranking metric (|log₂FC| × fraction of classes in which the gene was expressed) was computed to identify pan-retinal signatures versus cell-type-specific changes.

All analyses were executed on an HPC cluster via SLURM (`execution_mode = hpc_slurm`).

## 3. Results

### 3.1 Quality Control and Dataset Overview

After QC filtering, all 15,307 cells were retained (0.0% removed) and the gene space was reduced to 22,387 features. The DDX41 mutant arm (6,260 cells) showed higher mean detected genes (2,075.8) compared to WT (1,504.6), with a corresponding higher median (1,776.5 vs. 1,194.0). This difference in capture depth between arms is a technical observation that does not affect the log1p-normalized comparisons but is noted for transparency.

### 3.2 Cell Composition Shifts

| MG | 5.91 | 12.57 | 2.13× | +6.66 |

Neuroglial populations (MG, AC) expand substantially, while photoreceptor-adjacent classes (BC, Cone) contract. The Rod proportion remains essentially stable despite dramatic transcriptional changes (Section 3.4). Microglia show the largest proportional fold-change (3.62×) but from a very low baseline.
